claims.text: The deviation itself is established on the platform's own recorded distances: the trip record shows 13.2 km actually driven against a 12.0 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.20 km, which is above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so no part of this case can be disposed of as 'within tolerance'.

The GPS trace confirms which route was taken and when, as POL-RD-22 directs it be used: 49 fixes at 30 s with 100% coverage and no gaps show the vehicle off the recommended route from the first Braddell Road fix at 20:54:02 until it regained Serangoon Garden Way at 21:03:02, rejoining only at Upper Serangoon Road — the rider was carried on that unannounced stretch for roughly nine minutes before the route was rejoined.

The driver was never informed-notified in a form the policy accepts. POL-RD-21 allows notice of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally only where the trip call recording is the evidence. The chat log holds two messages only — the driver's 'At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' at 20:38:52 and the rider's reply at 20:39:12 — both timed to the pickup and neither referring to the CTE accident or to any reroute, while the route deviation was detected at 20:54:05. The trip record's in_app_calls list is empty, so no recording of any verbal notice exists, and POL-RD-21 states in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established.

The single rider message in the chat log is not the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 contemplates: 'ok' was sent at 20:39:12, about fifteen minutes before the deviation at 20:54:05, and answers a message about the pickup point, so it cannot be an assent to a reroute that had not yet happened and was never put to the rider.

Traffic justification is not made out on the record. POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; the advisory artifact records the overlap as true but its own derived field puts intersects_route at null and marks 'on the recommended route' as undetermined, supplying only road, direction and location. I do not ask the tribunal to place the accident from its own map-reading — the point is that the intersection element POL-RD-23 requires is left open by the very artifact that must carry it, so the reroute is not traffic-justified on this record.

Whichever way the traffic question falls, the money lands in the same place. Under POL-RD-24, row (b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km) and row (d) (not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km) both refund the excess distance fare in full; only row (a) reverses it, and row (a) requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, which the chat log and the empty call list do not support. The excess distance fare on POL-RD-24's formula is 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.86 SGD, without surge — precisely the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

The fare ledger shows the disputed amount has already moved: total charged 17.52 SGD with 0.86 SGD refunded and payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED. POL-GEN-03 defines that against the filing party, and the filer here is the driver, so his claim for the 0.86 SGD back fails and the present state — the rider not carrying that 0.86 SGD — stands.

If the tribunal were to treat the route-intersection question as genuinely open rather than answered against the driver, the fallback under POL-GEN-26 (and POL-RD-24's closing words for a case fitting no row) is escalation, and an escalated amount is held rather than collected — so the rider is still not made to pay the 0.86 SGD pending review.

There is no bar to the tribunal deciding this on the papers: the amount contested is 0.86 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no 0.95 confidence requirement is raised and POL-RD-25's 0.80 threshold for a route-deviation ruling is the only one that applies.

claims.text: The reroute was traffic-justified on this record, so the live rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix are (a) and (b), not (d). The traffic advisory records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23 to 21:40 on 9 Sep 2026, and ACCIDENT is an incident type POL-RD-23 counts as justifying a reroute; the trip window (20:40:02 to 21:04:02) sits wholly inside that validity window, and the derived block marks overlaps_trip_window true. The platform's own record shows the recommended route ran on the CTE and that the vehicle left it at the Braddell Road exit - the same road, direction and location_desc the advisory names - so the advisory answers the intersection question against the trip's own route and deviation event. I accept that the advisory artifact does not itself resolve intersection (its derived intersects_route is null and the record leaves that to the judge), but the fields it does carry are matched by the trip record's route and by the route_deviation_detected event at the PIE / CTE interchange (Braddell Road exit).

The fact the POL-RD-24 matrix turns on - whether the driver informed the rider of the deviation - cannot be established on this record, so POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated and the 0.86 SGD held rather than left refunded. The driver's case is a verbal notice acknowledged by a nod. POL-RD-21 admits verbal notice only where the trip call recording is in evidence, and this record carries no call at all: trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and POL-RD-21's own note C11 records that these records carry no call recordings. The chat log is complete (weight 1.0) and holds two messages, both before the trip started (20:38:52 and 20:39:12) and both about the pick-up point - neither mentions the deviation - and the trip record's messages_during_trip block is empty. So the driver's positive case fails under POL-RD-21. But POL-RD-21 says a verbal notice with no recording 'cannot be established'; it does not say the notice was not given, and the rider's denial is his own uncorroborated statement, which nothing independent in the record contradicts. POL-RD-24 closes by escalating a case that fits no row, and POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' as exactly the kind of fact that, being unestablished, sends the case to a human reviewer.

The 0.86 SGD is expressly interim and not a final determination, so nothing in the record supports simply leaving it where it stands. The platform's own event entry reads 'Interim adjustment after a rider route complaint: SGD 0.86 refunded to rider and recovered from driver earnings pending review', and the fare breakdown still shows payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 0.86. POL-GEN-03 provides that an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and the amount is held - which is precisely the unsettled state this interim adjustment is already in pending the human review POL-GEN-26 requires. Holding the amount is the outcome that does not finally take 0.86 SGD from the driver's earnings on a fact the record cannot establish.

If any money is to move, the record fixes its ceiling at the excess distance fare and no more. The deviation is 1.20 km - the platform's recorded actual route distance of 13.2 km less the recommended 12.0 km, the two recorded distances POL-RD-22 directs be used - and at the recorded rate of 0.72 SGD per km that is 0.86 SGD, rounded to the cent under POL-RD-24. There is nothing to add: surge_amount is 0.00 and tolls_erp is 0.00. That figure is exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, so the driver's exposure on this trip is capped at 0.86 SGD and no further recovery from his earnings is supported by the record.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this ends in NO_ACTION — the present state stands and neither amount moves.

Where the money figures come from. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05017) gives a recorded actual distance of 13.2 km against a recommended 12.0 km, so the deviation is 1.20 km (POL-RD-22), above the 1.0 km tolerance. At the recorded rate of 0.72 SGD per km, POL-RD-24's excess distance fare is 1.20 x 0.72 = 0.86 SGD, with no surge; the fare ledger (EV-FARE-05017) shows exactly that 0.86 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver, out of a total charge of 17.52 SGD.

Was the reroute justified? Yes — and that does not help the driver here. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05017-01) records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23–21:40, which covers the whole trip window 20:40:02–21:04:02; the recommended route ran on the CTE past that exit and the trip record shows the vehicle left it at that point. ACCIDENT is an incident type POL-RD-23 accepts, so the reroute was traffic-justified (the rider's contrary claim on this point is not accepted — but, as the rider also notes, it changes nothing, because the only other row open on these facts, (d), refunds the same sum).

Was the rider told? No — and this decides the case. POL-RD-21 requires notice of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05017) is complete and holds only the driver's pick-up note at 20:38:52 and the rider's 'ok' at 20:39:12, both about the pick-up point and fifteen minutes before the deviation was detected at 20:54:05; the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty. The 'ok' is not the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 requires, and a verbal warning with no recording cannot be established (POL-RD-21). The case therefore falls in row (b) of POL-RD-24 — traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare.

Why NO_ACTION. The rider is owed the 0.86 SGD, and that is precisely the sum the platform already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver. The driver filed to contest it. Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is read against the filing party: the driver's claim fails against the present state, so the ruling is NO_ACTION and neither amount moves. The 0.86 SGD refund stands.

On the driver's escalation argument. I do not escalate under POL-GEN-26. That clause is for a fact the record leaves open; here POL-RD-21 supplies the rule for an unrecorded verbal warning and row (b) is the row for a rider not informed, so the informing question is settled rather than open. In any event the money is the same either way, so escalation would only hold an amount that is already correct.

On confidence. The contested sum, 0.86 SGD, is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the AI may decide; POL-RD-25's 0.80 threshold is met (0.85), and its 2 km limb does not apply (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false). The artifacts carrying the deciding facts all sit at weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
Mr D-59211 (driver) filed to get back the 0.86 SGD Ryde refunded to Ms R-86387 (rider) and recovered from his earnings after her route complaint. The claim fails: the rider is owed that 0.86 SGD, so the present state stands and no money moves in either direction.

Deviation. On the platform's recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 directs be used, the trip was 13.2 km against a 12.0 km recommended route (EV-TRIP-05017) — 1.20 km over, above the 1.0 km tolerance. No part of this case can be disposed of as 'within tolerance'.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05017-01) records an ACCIDENT on the CTE towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23–21:40 on 9 Sep 2026, and it overlaps the trip window (20:40:02–21:04:02). Its derived block leaves the route-intersection question to me. On the road, direction and location it carries — CTE, towards SLE, after the Braddell Road exit — it sits on the stretch of CTE the recommended route uses, at the very exit where the trip record shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at 20:54:05. I find the reroute traffic-justified. The rider's contrary argument (intersects_route is null and the element is left open by the artifact) is noted, but it does not change the money: as set out below, the 'not justified' row pays exactly the same sum.

Notice to the rider (POL-RD-21). POL-RD-21 accepts notice of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally only where the trip call recording is in evidence. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05017, weight 1.0) holds exactly two messages, both about the pickup point and both sent before the trip began (20:38:52 and 20:39:12); the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty and its messages_during_trip block is empty. POL-RD-21 states in terms that a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established, so Mr D-59211's verbal-notice account does not establish the notice the clause requires, and the rider's 'ok' at 20:39:12 — about fifteen minutes before the deviation — cannot be an assent to a reroute not yet put to him. The rider was not informed in the form the policy accepts.

Outcome (POL-RD-24). The applicable row is (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare. POL-RD-24's formula gives 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.86 SGD, without surge (surge_amount 0.00, tolls_erp 0.00). Had the traffic question gone the other way, row (d) pays the identical 0.86 SGD, so the money does not turn on it. That 0.86 SGD has already been refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver: EV-FARE-05017 shows refund_issued_sgd 0.86 and payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, and the fare_adjusted event of 2026-09-10T03:30:02 records the same. The rider is owed it and the driver is not owed it back. Read against the filing party, as POL-GEN-03 requires, the driver's claim fails and the state stands: NO_ACTION.

On the driver's escalation argument (POL-GEN-26). The driver says the fact 'was the rider informed' cannot be established, so the case must go to a human and the 0.86 SGD held. POL-GEN-26 fires where the evidence that would carry a needed fact is missing or impaired. Here it is neither: the chat log is complete and unimpaired at weight 1.0, and this record type carries no call recordings (POL-RD-21 note C11), so the empty call list is the record's true state rather than an impaired one. The fact is therefore determinable, and it resolves against the driver. This is a decidable case, not an open one, and the interim refund does not need a human to settle it.

On the rider's fallback (escalate if the route-intersection question is genuinely open). The intersection is determinable from the advisory's own road, direction and location, as above; and even if it were not, rows (b) and (d) pay the same 0.86 SGD, so no escalation follows.

Who decides, and confidence (POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25). The amount contested is 0.86 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence provided POL-RD-25's 0.80 is met; neither profile carries a fraud flag. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-05017, EV-FARE-05017, EV-CHAT-05017, EV-ADVIS-05017-01) has weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0. My confidence is 0.9, above the 0.80 bar.

No referral follows: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalation issues no monetary outcome and the amount is held: the 0.86 SGD interim adjustment (already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings) stays where it is, neither collected nor refunded, pending review. Both money fields are therefore null.

What the record settles. The deviation is 1.20 km - the platform's recorded actual distance of 13.2 km less the recorded recommended distance of 12.0 km (POL-RD-22, EV-TRIP-05017) - which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The excess distance fare is 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.86 SGD, rounded to the cent (POL-RD-24, EV-FARE-05017), and that is exactly the sum already moved. The driver's point that the record fixes the ceiling at 0.86 SGD and no more is accepted; there is nothing to add, as surge and ERP are nil.

The reroute was traffic-justified. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05017-01) records an ACCIDENT - an 'incident' type POL-RD-23 counts - on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23-21:40 on 9 Sep, which covers the whole trip window (20:40:02-21:04:02). The recommended route ran on the CTE and the vehicle left it at the Braddell Road exit, precisely where the advisory sits, so the advisory intersects the recommended route as POL-RD-23 requires. I do not accept the rider's argument that traffic justification fails merely because the artifact's own derived field leaves intersects_route null: POL-RD-23 hands that determination to the tribunal on the advisory's road, direction and location, and all three match the trip's route and deviation event.

What the record cannot settle. POL-RD-21 permits notice of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally only where the trip call recording is in evidence. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05017) holds two messages, both at 20:38-20:39 and both about the pick-up point, neither about the deviation detected at 20:54:05; the trip record's in_app_calls list is empty, so no recording of any verbal notice exists; and the rider denies being told. POL-RD-21 states in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established, and POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' as a fact that, where the record cannot establish it, sends the case to a human reviewer.

Because that fact is unestablished, no row of the POL-RD-24 matrix fits. Row (a) needs the rider informed and agreed; row (b) needs the rider not informed. Neither can be found: the driver's claimed verbal notice is not established, and the rider's denial is his own uncorroborated account, which does not affirmatively establish the negative. Row (d) does not apply because the reroute was traffic-justified. POL-RD-24 closes by escalating a case that fits no row, and POL-GEN-26 requires it.

On the remaining claims: the deviation and the route taken are established (rider, accepted; the GPS trace, 49 fixes at 30 s, 100% coverage, is used only as POL-RD-22 directs, not to re-measure distance); the rider's 'ok' at 20:39:12 is not the acknowledgment POL-RD-21 contemplates, being fifteen minutes before the deviation and answering a pick-up message (rider, accepted); the rider's case that the money lands in the same place whichever way the traffic question falls (rider, rejected) holds only if the notice fact is resolved one way or the other, and it is not; that the 0.86 SGD adjustment is expressly interim and pending review (driver, accepted); and that there is no bar to a ruling on the papers at 0.86 SGD with no fraud flag (rider, accepted) - the escalation here rests on POL-GEN-26, not on any POL-GEN-22 or POL-RD-25 confidence bar.

Open question for the reviewer: on the evidence, was the rider informed of the deviation before or at the point of deviation? The chat and call record cannot say, and the parties' accounts conflict. No referral attaches, as the route-deviation policy provides none.

ruling.explanation:
To driver D-59211 and rider R-86387. I am sending this to a human reviewer rather than deciding it, because one fact the route-deviation rules need cannot be established from the record, and the rules make that an escalation (POL-GEN-26).

What is settled. The deviation is 1.20 km: the trip record's recorded actual distance of 13.2 km less its recorded recommended distance of 12.0 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22; EV-TRIP-05017). The reroute was traffic-justified (POL-RD-23): the LTA advisory records an accident on the Central Expressway towards SLE after the Braddell Road exit, valid 20:23 to 21:40 on 9 Sep 2026 (EV-ADVIS-05017-01), which covers the trip window of 20:40:02 to 21:04:02 and, by its road, direction and location, lies on the CTE stretch the recommended route used and which the vehicle left at the Braddell Road exit. The advisory's own derived block leaves the route-intersection question to the Judge, and on those fields I find the reroute justified. That places the case in the traffic-justified half of POL-RD-24's matrix, not the 'within tolerance' rows.

What is not settled. Whether the driver informed the rider of the deviation. The in-app chat log is complete and holds only two messages before the trip started — the driver's 'At Dempsey Block 8 drop off' at 20:38:52 and the rider's 'ok' at 20:39:12 — neither touching the diversion; the trip record's in-app call list is empty, so no call recording exists (EV-CHAT-05017, EV-TRIP-05017). The driver relies on a verbal notice acknowledged by a nod. POL-RD-21 admits a verbal notice only where the trip call recording is the evidence, and states in terms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The rider's account that he was told nothing is his own statement, and POL-RD-21 does not make a counterparty statement the test for this limb, so it does not decide the other way either. The fact therefore cannot be established.

Consequence. POL-RD-24's matrix needs this fact: row (a) (no refund) requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, and row (b) (refund) requires that he was not informed. Neither can be found on the record, so the case fits no row, and POL-RD-24 and POL-GEN-26 send it to human review. The 0.86 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver stays held exactly as the platform left it — it was itself an interim adjustment 'pending review' (EV-FARE-05017, fare_adjusted at 2026-09-10T03:30:02) — and this ruling moves no money.

The figures used. The excess distance fare is 1.20 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.864, rounded to 0.86 SGD (POL-RD-24; EV-FARE-05017); that is the sum already refunded and the ceiling on any recovery (surge 0.00, tolls 0.00). Both sides agree on that arithmetic; they differ only on whether the refund is due, which is the fact left open. If the reviewer finds the driver did inform the rider and the rider agreed, row (a) gives no refund; if the reviewer finds the rider was not informed, or the reroute not justified, rows (b)/(d) confirm the 0.86 SGD refund. Because the driver filed to contest a refund already issued and recovered, a finding that the rider is owed it makes the outcome NO_ACTION with both amounts null, and a finding that the driver is owed it makes it DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 0.86 SGD. The confidence bar is met (dispute value 0.86 SGD is below 10.00 SGD under POL-GEN-22, neither profile carries a fraud flag, and POL-RD-25 applies), so the escalation here rests on the unestablished fact, not on confidence. A route deviation has no referral clause in this version, so I add none; the open question above belongs in the reviewer's file.
